messages:
Marta: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal: instead of shipping client SDK shims for v2->v3, add a tiny middleware at the edge that rewrites incoming v2 requests to the v3 shape and vice-versa for responses. Keeps runtime changes centralized and avoids constant client patches.
Devon: Short question — how tiny is "tiny"? does this live in our gateway or in a sidecar?
Marta: Gateway middleware first. Goal: <100 LOC transform layer that handles header negotiation + a couple of payload shape diffs. No ML changes.
Kevin: Concern: latency and coupling to gateway rollout. If gateway touches every request, we need perf numbers.
Sasha: Perf + safety: can we make it opt-in per-tenant? feature-flagged header like `X-RW-Compat: v2` so only tenants opting in pay the cost.
Marta: Yes — header opt-in, and we add tenant routing so dedicated customers can bypass middleware entirely.
Devon: What about streaming? v2 clients use chunked frames; v3 uses structured events. Transforming streaming is messy.
Marta: For streaming we plan to 1) support only unary calls in middleware initially, 2) for streaming require client-side adapter or tenant-side gateway route. We document it.
Kevin: Can we handle simple field renames and envelope wrapping/unwrapping? those are low-cost.
Marta: Exactly — envelope around `input` -> `messages` etc. We'll implement mapping table and a small serializer.
Sasha: Safety net: add an errors header when we rewrite so we can detect silent regressions. e.g., `X-RW-Compat-Transform: ok|warn|fail`.
Marta: Good. Also telemetry: increment counters per tenant + rewrite type. We can reuse existing observability tags.
Devon: How do we test regressions? who owns QA?
Marta: Plan: nightly e2e with recorded v2 client traces replayed through middleware into v3 model, diff top-level artifacts. Add canary rollouts.
Kevin: Who owns deployment? gateway infra or compat team?
Marta: Gateway infra builds + we've agreed compat team writes the transform rules and tests. infra will review and deploy.
Sasha: If we ship this, we should also add an escape hatch: `X-RW-Compat: bypass` to force passthrough for debugging.
Marta: Agreed. Also TTL on the feature-flag so we can sunet once migration complete.
deploy-bot: Deployment plan ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/COMPAT-211 — staged rollout to <us-east-1> first.
Marta: Action items: (1) Sasha to draft transform mapping spreadsheet, (2) Kevin to run perf microbench against gateway stub, (3) Devon to prototype header negotiation patch. I'll own RFC update and canary playbook.
Sasha: I'll drop the mapping in the RFC doc by EOD tomorrow.
Kevin: Starting perf run now, will post numbers in this thread.
Devon: I'll push a tiny PoC to `compat/middleware-proto` and ping for review.
Marta: Thanks — goal is lower friction migration for customers without increasing client churn. We'll iterate after canary. :thumbsup:
